headline: Denied $249,708 HHS Lease funding, voted to reconsider pension increase for Vincent Fernandez, and accepted deed for 161 Totman Street.
summary: The council denied a $249,708 supplemental appropriation for the HHS lease and voted 7-4 to reconsider a pension increase and back pay for Vincent Fernandez, referring the matter to the City Manager. It accepted a deed for 161 Totman Street, approved a license agreement with The Chiropractic Healing Center, and added Woburn St sidewalks to the 2028 Capital Plan. Numerous requests on zoning, traffic, parks, monuments, and utility pole installations were referred to city departments or scheduled for public hearings, and a motion to release Executive Session minutes on the UHC-TIF was defeated.
decisions: Withdrew the zoning ordinance on curb cuts and referred it to the Planning Board, with a public hearing set for September 22, 2026.
Referred National Grid's request to install a utility pole at Westford Street and 15 Technology Drive to the Wire Inspector.
Referred National Grid's request to install utility poles at 1270 and 1299 Westford Street to the Wire Inspector.

Adopted a motion to reconsider the July 14, 2026 vote authorizing special legislation to increase the pension and provide 10 years back pay for Vincent Fernandez, 7-4, and referred the matter to the City Manager.
Referred a request to evaluate and repair the dangerous condition on Gage Street and the overgrown UML parcel abutting it to the City Manager.
Referred a request for an update on zoning laws for data centers to the City Manager.
C. Rourke withdrew a motion to pilot holding council meetings every two weeks with subcommittees on alternating Tuesdays.
Referred a request for an update on swapping volleyball surface material at Gage and a seasonal restroom facility to the City Manager.
Referred a request for funding options to update the McPherson swimming pool facility to the City Manager.
Referred a request to establish standard operating procedures for maintaining, testing, opening, closing, and winterizing aquatic recreational facilities to the City Manager.
Referred a request to assess tenant displacement and a local Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act (TOPA) to the City Manager.
Referred a request to create interpretive materials for immigrant and cultural monuments around City Hall Plaza to the City Manager.
Referred a request for an update on repaving and traffic calming on Andover Street and the western half of Douglas Road to the City Manager.
Referred a request for an update on pickleball court plans, including at Shedd Park, to the City Manager.
Referred a request to increase police traffic enforcement on Stevens Street to the City Manager.
Referred a request to evaluate a residential front-yard de-paving and re-greening pilot program with a homeowner rebate to the City Manager.
Defeated a motion to release the July 14, 2026 Executive Session minutes on the UHC-TIF and hold further discussion in open session, 5-6.
Adopted a request to look at funding sources to reinstall the wrought iron fence around the Ladd and Whitney Monument, 6-5, and referred it to the City Manager.
Referred a request for a schedule of crosswalk painting around schools and main roads to the City Manager.
Defeated a motion to accept and place on file the Motion Response on Parking Enforcement at Schools, 4-7.
Adopted a motion to place the Woburn St sidewalks item on the 2028 Capital Plan, 11-0.
Accepted and placed on file the Motion Response providing an update on E Street.
Accepted and placed on file the Motion Response on Injury Coverage Policies.
Accepted and placed on file the Motion Response on Lowell being named 2026 Best Place to Live in MA.
Accepted and placed on file the Motion Response on the Invitation to Olympians.
Accepted and placed on file the Motion Response on Kerouac Park Restoration.
Accepted and placed on file the Motion Response on Fire Dept OT Spending.
Accepted and placed on file the Quarter Two Motion Update informational report.
Adopted the vote to accept the deed for 161 Totman Street, 10-0 with 1 absent.
Adopted the vote authorizing the City Manager to enter a license agreement with The Chiropractic Healing Center, P.C., 11-0.
Adopted the vote to authorize payment of bills incurred in excess of appropriations, 11-0.
Adopted the vote to designate the LHS Wrestling Room as a polling location, 10-0 with 1 absent.
Denied a motion to transfer $249,708 as a supplemental appropriation for the HHS Lease, despite 7 yeas to 4 nays.
Referred the ordinance amending Chapter 266-61 on Space Savers to a public hearing on August 11, 2026.
Adopted the resolution recognizing Lowell's Bicentennial Celebration, 11-0.
Continued the Non-Profit Organization Subcommittee matter to the next meeting.
Accepted and adopted the Wire Inspector orders for National Grid pole work at multiple streets.
Referred a property damage claim to the Law Department.
Referred Nathalie Amador's request for a handicap parking sign at 47 Walnut Street to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Jacquelin Tanguay's request for a handicap parking sign at 220 River Road to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Benjamin Opikhara's request for an 'Autistic Child' sign at 45 Willard Street to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace 180 feet of low-pressure gas main on Florence Avenue to a public hearing on August 11, 2026.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace 270 feet of low-pressure gas main on Nottingham Street and Thompson Court to a public hearing on August 11, 2026.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace 590 feet of low-pressure gas main on Marshall and McIntyre Streets to a public hearing on August 11, 2026.
Referred National Grid's request to install a JO Pole at 93 Mammoth Road to a public hearing on August 11, 2026.
Referred National Grid's request to install a JO Pole at 117-125 Perry Street to a public hearing on August 11, 2026.

Mercier commented on prior vote noting she did not have proper facts and 
that there should be information provided to have a more informed vote.  C.

In City Council, seconded by C. Mercier, referred to City Manager.  So

6.7. C. Robinson / C. Scott - Req the City Manager have the proper 
department establish a set of SOP’s for maintaining, testing, opening, 
closing, and winterizing all aquatic recreational facilities throughout 
the city including timelines.
In City Council, no second needed, referred to City Manager.  So voted.  C. 
Robinson noted the need for proper procedures to protect assets.  C. Scott 
noted the need to know of any issues well before use of these assets.  
6.8. C. Liang - Req. City Mgr. assess the prevalence of tenant 
displacement and the potential impacts of implementing a local 
version of the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act (TOPA).
In City Council, seconded by C. McDonough, referred to City Manager.  So 
voted.  C. Liang noted the need to assist with home ownership and the 
issue with tenants being displaced due to actions of realtors and owners.  
M. Gitschier noted it was HB-1544 and that a letter of support could be sent
to the delegation.  C. McDonough noted the problem in the community and 
that there is also a lack of inspections being done at these sites.  C. Juran 
commented on the coverage of the proposed act and that it is still too early 
to support legislation as it is being developed.

appropriate department and community partners to create interpretive

Street and the western half of Douglas Road.
In City Council, seconded by C. Mercier, referred to City Manager.  So 
voted.  C. Juran noted the importance of providing information to citizens.

update on plans for pickleball courts at parks around the city 
(including at Shedd Park), including fencing to ensure that courts are 
properly separated from each other.
In City Council, seconded by C. Chau, referred to City Manager.  So voted. 
C. Juran noted it was a fast-growing sport and that demand has increased.  
C. Juran noted importance to separate the playing surfaces on the courts.  
C. McDonough opposed the Shedd Park location.  C. Robinson noted some
concerns with noise regarding the sport but indicated that there are ways to
mitigate that.  C. Liang could not see it at Shedd Park as the tennis courts

6.12. C. Chau - Req. City Mgr. have Police Department increase traffic 
enforcement on Stevens Street.
In City Council, seconded by C. Liang, referred to City Manager.  So voted. 
C. Chau noted work being done and that it will resolve some issues like 
speeding.  C. Descoteaux commented on the issues in the neighborhood.

6.13. C. Chau - Req. City Mgr. direct appropriate departments to 
evaluate the feasibility of a residential front-yard de-paving and re-
greening pilot program to reduce urban heat island effects and 
stormwater runoff, that includes a homeowner rebate component.
In City Council, seconded by C. Nuon, referred to City Manager.  So voted. 
C. Chau noted the need to create open green space.  C. Juran commented 
the need to ensure such changes are done in a proper ecological manner.  
C. Scott noted the need to enforce rules against those who pave their entire
yard.  
6.14. M. Gitschier - Req. the minutes of the July 14, 2026 Executive 
Session be released regarding the UHC-TIF; once released all 
discussion to be held in open session for this topic.
In City Council, seconded by C. Robinson, referred to City Manager.  
Motion by C. Robinson, seconded by C. Mercier to accept and release 
Executive Session minutes regarding UHC-TIF and allow further discussion
in open session.  Defeated  per Roll Call vote 5 yeas (C. Chau, M. 
Gitschier, C. McDonough, C. Robinson, C. Scott), 6 nays (C. Descoteaux, 
C. Juran, C. Liang, C. Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Rourke).  So voted.  C. Juran 
noted minutes addressed other topics and that the matter was still in 
negotiations.  Chair relinquished to Vice Chair Nuon at 8:35 PM.  M. 
Gitschier noted there was no harm to release minutes as the public has a 
right to know where their money is going.  Chair returned at 8:37 PM.  C. 
Nuon noted the need to keep in session as discussions continue regarding 
TIF agreement.  C. McDonough noted if a public discussion is proper as the
minutes have not been released.  City Solicitor Williams noted that body 
can vote to release the minutes, but issue would be that negotiations are 
on-going.  C. Nuon noted if open discussion with one developer is allowed 
then it should apply to all developers and that is not a good practice.  M. 
Gitschier noted that information was originally provided to Council publicly.  
C. Scott noted there should be no issues as negotiating parties are both 
public entities.  City Solicitor Williams indicated that status of parties would 
not affect the analysis.  Chair relinquished to Vice Chair Nuon at 8:45 PM.

to hide it.  C. Mercier noted the need for negotiations to be complete.  Chair
returned at 8:47 PM.  C. Descoteaux noted review of minutes which 
indicate matter is not completed.  C. Liang noted if allowed there would be 
no reason to have executive sessions.  C. McDonough requested solicitor

as documents.  
6.15. M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. look at funding sources to reinstall 
the wrought iron fence back around the Ladd and Whitney Monument.
In City Council, seconded by C. Robinson, referred to City Manager.  
Adopted per Roll Call vote 6 yeas (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, 
C. Mercier, C. Robinson, C. Rourke), 5 nays (C. Juran, C. Liang, C. 
McDonough, C. Nuon, C. Scott).  So voted.  Chair relinquished to Vice 
Chair Nuon at 8:54 PM.  M. Gitschier outlined the history of the monument 
and that it is a grave site as well and that the structure must be preserved.  
Chair returned at 8:57 PM.  C. Robinson noted how other communities 
fence their monuments.  C. Rourke noted the need to distinguish this 
monument.  Motion by C. Nuon, seconded by C. McDonough to suspend 
rules to allow Joseph Boyle to address the body.  So voted.  Mr. Boyle 
noted he was in favor of protecting the grave.  C. Nuon noted the need to 
honor and respect the monument.  C. Mercier must protect and honor site.  
C. Juran questioned placement of fence.  M. Gitschier noted it would be 
around the whole area as it was historically done.  C. McDonough noted 
support for fencing and concern is with location.  C. Chau questioned if 
CPA could be a funding source.  C. McDonough would not support the 
whole island as it eliminates access to green space.  C. Nuon noted the use
of site as a protest area.  C. Mercier noted access should be allowed for 
some activities.  M. Gitschier noted motion is to fund for whole area.  
6.16. M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. provide a schedule to the City 
Council for the crosswalks painting around the schools and main 
roads.
In City Council, seconded by C. Nuon, referred to City Manager.  So voted.
